12: /-!
13: # Quotienting out a free `ℤ`-module
14: 
15: If `G` is a rank `d` free `ℤ`-module, then `G/nG` is a finite group of cardinality `n ^ d`.
16: -/
17: 
18: @[expose] public section
19: 
20: open Finsupp Function Module
21: 
22: variable {G H M : Type*} [AddCommGroup G] {n : ℕ}
23: 
24: variable (G n) in
25: /-- `ModN G n` denotes the quotient of `G` by multiples of `n` -/
26: abbrev ModN : Type _ := G ⧸ LinearMap.range (LinearMap.lsmul ℤ G n)
27: 
28: namespace ModN
29: 
30: instance : Module (ZMod n) (ModN G n) := QuotientAddGroup.zmodModule (by simp)
31: 
32: set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
33: /-- The universal property of `ModN G n` in terms of monoids: Monoid homomorphisms from `ModN G n`
34: are the same as monoid homomorphisms from `G` whose values are `n`-torsion. -/
35: protected def liftEquiv [AddMonoid M] : (ModN G n →+ M) ≃ {φ : G →+ M // ∀ g, n • φ g = 0} where
36:   toFun f := ⟨f.comp (QuotientAddGroup.mk' _), fun g ↦ by
37:     let Gn : AddSubgroup G := (LinearMap.range (LinearMap.lsmul ℤ G n)).toAddSubgroup
38:     suffices n • g ∈ (QuotientAddGroup.mk' Gn).ker by
39:       simp only [AddMonoidHom.coe_comp, comp_apply, ← map_nsmul]
40:       change f (QuotientAddGroup.mk' Gn (n • g)) = 0 -- Can we avoid `change`?
41:       rw [this, map_zero]
42:     simp [QuotientAddGroup.ker_mk', Gn]⟩
43:   invFun φ := QuotientAddGroup.lift _ φ <| by rintro - ⟨g, rfl⟩; simpa using φ.property g
44:   left_inv f := by
45:     ext x
46:     induction x using QuotientAddGroup.induction_on
47:     rfl -- Should `simp` suffice here?
48:   right_inv φ := by aesop
49: 
50: /-- The universal property of `ModN G n` in terms of `ZMod n`-modules: `ZMod n`-linear maps from
51: `ModN G n` are the same as monoid homomorphisms from `G` whose values are `n`-torsion. -/
52: protected def liftEquiv' [AddCommGroup H] [Module (ZMod n) H] :
53:     (ModN G n →ₗ[ZMod n] H) ≃ {φ : G →+ H // ∀ g, n • φ g = 0} :=
54:   (AddMonoidHom.toZModLinearMapEquiv n).symm.toEquiv.trans ModN.liftEquiv
55: 
56: variable (n) in
57: /-- The quotient map `G → G / nG`. -/
58: def mkQ : G →+ ModN G n := (LinearMap.range (LinearMap.lsmul ℤ G n)).mkQ
59: 
60: variable [NeZero n]
61: 
62: set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
63: /-- Given a free module `G` over `ℤ`, construct the corresponding basis
64: of `G / ⟨n⟩` over `ℤ / nℤ`. -/
65: noncomputable def basis {ι : Type*} (b : Basis ι ℤ G) : Basis ι (ZMod n) (ModN G n) := by
66:   set ψ : G →+ G := zsmulAddGroupHom n
67:   set nG := LinearMap.range (LinearMap.lsmul ℤ G n)
68:   set H := G ⧸ nG
69:   set φ : G →ₗ[ℤ] H := nG.mkQ
70:   let mod : (ι →₀ ℤ) →ₗ[ℤ] (ι →₀ ZMod n) := mapRange.linearMap (Int.castAddHom _).toIntLinearMap
71:   let f : G →ₗ[ℤ] (ι →₀ ℤ) := b.repr
72:   have hker : nG ≤ LinearMap.ker (mod.comp f) := by
73:     rintro _ ⟨x, rfl⟩
74:     ext b
75:     simp [mod, f]
76:   let g : H →ₗ[ℤ] (ι →₀ ZMod n) := nG.liftQ (mod.comp f) hker
77:   refine ⟨.ofBijective (g.toAddMonoidHom.toZModLinearMap n) ⟨?_, ?_⟩⟩
78:   · rw [AddMonoidHom.coe_toZModLinearMap, LinearMap.toAddMonoidHom_coe, injective_iff_map_eq_zero,
79:       nG.mkQ_surjective.forall]
80:     intro x hx
81:     simp only [Submodule.mkQ_apply, g] at hx
82:     rw [Submodule.liftQ_apply] at hx
83:     replace hx : ∀ b, ↑n ∣ f x b := by
84:       simpa [mod, DFunLike.ext_iff, ZMod.intCast_zmod_eq_zero_iff_dvd] using! hx
85:     simp only [Submodule.mkQ_apply]
86:     rw [Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero]
87:     choose c hc using hx
88:     refine ⟨b.repr.symm ⟨(f x).support, c, by simp [hc, NeZero.ne]⟩, b.repr.injective ?_⟩
89:     simpa [DFunLike.ext_iff, eq_comm] using! hc
90:   · suffices mod ∘ b.repr = g ∘ nG.mkQ by
91:       exact (this ▸ (mapRange_surjective _ (map_zero _) ZMod.intCast_surjective).comp
92:         b.repr.surjective).of_comp
93:     ext x b
94:     simp [mod, g, f, H]
95: 
96: set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
97: lemma basis_apply_eq_mkQ {ι : Type*} (b : Basis ι ℤ G) (i : ι) : basis b i = mkQ n (b i) := by
98:   rw [Basis.apply_eq_iff]; simp [basis, mkQ]
99: 
100: variable [Module.Free ℤ G] [Module.Finite ℤ G]
101: 
102: instance instModuleFinite : Module.Finite (ZMod n) (ModN G n) :=
103:   .of_basis <| basis <| Module.Free.chooseBasis ℤ G
104: 
105: instance instFinite : Finite (ModN G n) := Module.finite_of_finite (ZMod n)
106: 
107: variable (G n)
108: @[simp] lemma natCard_eq : Nat.card (ModN G n) = n ^ Module.finrank ℤ G := by
109:   simp [Nat.card_congr (basis <| Module.Free.chooseBasis ℤ G).repr.toEquiv,
110:     Nat.card_eq_fintype_card, Module.finrank_eq_card_chooseBasisIndex]
111: 
112: end ModN

11: /-!
12: # The `A`-module structure on `M ⊗[R] N`
13: 
14: When `M` is both an `R`-module and an `A`-module, and `Algebra R A`, then many of the morphisms
15: preserve the actions by `A`.
16: 
17: The `Module` instance itself is provided elsewhere as `TensorProduct.leftModule`. This file provides
18: more general versions of the definitions already in `LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct`.
19: 
20: In this file, we use the convention that `M`, `N`, `P`, `Q` are all `R`-modules, but only `M` and
21: `P` are simultaneously `A`-modules.
22: 
23: ## Main definitions
24: 
25: * `TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.curry`
26: * `TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.uncurry`
27: * `TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.lcurry`
28: * `TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.lift`
29: * `TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.lift.equiv`
30: * `TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.mk`
31: * `TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.map`
32: * `TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.mapBilinear`
33: * `TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.congr`
34: * `TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.rid`
35: * `TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.homTensorHomMap`
36: * `TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.assoc`
37: * `TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.leftComm`
38: * `TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.rightComm`
39: * `TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.tensorTensorTensorComm`
40: * `LinearMap.baseChange A f` is the `A`-linear map `A ⊗ f`, for an `R`-linear map `f`.
41: 
42: ## Implementation notes
43: 
44: We could thus consider replacing the less general definitions with these ones. If we do this, we
45: probably should still implement the less general ones as abbreviations to the more general ones with
46: fewer type arguments.
47: -/

78: /-- Heterobasic version of `TensorProduct.curry`:
79: 
80: Given a linear map `M ⊗[R] N →[A] P`, compose it with the canonical
81: bilinear map `M →[A] N →[R] M ⊗[R] N` to form a bilinear map `M →[A] N →[R] P`. -/
82: @[simps]
83: nonrec def curry (f : M ⊗[R] N →ₗ[A] P) : M →ₗ[A] N →ₗ[R] P :=
84:   { curry (f.restrictScalars R) with
85:     toFun := curry (f.restrictScalars R)
86:     map_smul' := fun c x => LinearMap.ext fun y => f.map_smul c (x ⊗ₜ y) }
87: 
88: theorem restrictScalars_curry (f : M ⊗[R] N →ₗ[A] P) :
89:     restrictScalars R (curry f) = TensorProduct.curry (f.restrictScalars R) :=
90:   rfl
91: 
92: /-- Just as `TensorProduct.ext` is marked `ext` instead of `TensorProduct.ext'`, this is
93: a better `ext` lemma than `TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.ext` below.
94: 
95: See note [partially-applied ext lemmas]. -/
96: @[ext high]
97: nonrec theorem curry_injective : Function.Injective (curry : (M ⊗ N →ₗ[A] P) → M →ₗ[A] N →ₗ[R] P) :=
98:   fun _ _ h =>
99:   LinearMap.restrictScalars_injective R <|
100:     curry_injective <| (congr_arg (LinearMap.restrictScalars R) h :)
101: 
102: theorem ext {g h : M ⊗[R] N →ₗ[A] P} (H : ∀ x y, g (x ⊗ₜ y) = h (x ⊗ₜ y)) : g = h :=
103:   curry_injective <| LinearMap.ext₂ H

105: /-- Heterobasic version of `TensorProduct.lift`:
106: 
107: Constructing a linear map `M ⊗[R] N →[A] P` given a bilinear map `M →[A] N →[R] P` with the
108: property that its composition with the canonical bilinear map `M →[A] N →[R] M ⊗[R] N` is
109: the given bilinear map `M →[A] N →[R] P`. -/
110: nonrec def lift (f : M →ₗ[A] N →ₗ[R] P) : M ⊗[R] N →ₗ[A] P :=
111:   { lift (f.restrictScalars R) with
112:     map_smul' := fun c =>
113:       show
114:         ∀ x : M ⊗[R] N,
115:           (lift (f.restrictScalars R)).comp (lsmul R R _ c) x =
116:             (lsmul R R _ c).comp (lift (f.restrictScalars R)) x
117:         from
118:         LinearMap.ext_iff.1 <|
119:           TensorProduct.ext' fun x y => by
120:             simp only [comp_apply, Algebra.lsmul_coe, smul_tmul', lift.tmul,
121:               coe_restrictScalars, f.map_smul, smul_apply] }

124: theorem lift_apply (f : M →ₗ[A] N →ₗ[R] P) (a : M ⊗[R] N) :
125:     AlgebraTensorModule.lift f a = TensorProduct.lift (LinearMap.restrictScalars R f) a :=
126:   rfl

129: theorem lift_tmul (f : M →ₗ[A] N →ₗ[R] P) (x : M) (y : N) : lift f (x ⊗ₜ y) = f x y :=
130:   rfl

136: 
137: /-- Heterobasic version of `TensorProduct.uncurry`:
138: 
139: Linearly constructing a linear map `M ⊗[R] N →[A] P` given a bilinear map `M →[A] N →[R] P`
140: with the property that its composition with the canonical bilinear map `M →[A] N →[R] M ⊗[R] N` is
141: the given bilinear map `M →[A] N →[R] P`. -/
142: @[simps]
143: def uncurry : (M →ₗ[A] N →ₗ[R] P) →ₗ[B] M ⊗[R] N →ₗ[A] P where
144:   toFun := lift
145:   map_add' _ _ := ext fun x y => by simp only [lift_tmul, add_apply]
146:   map_smul' _ _ := ext fun x y => by simp only [lift_tmul, smul_apply, RingHom.id_apply]
147: 
148: /-- Heterobasic version of `TensorProduct.lcurry`:
149: 
150: Given a linear map `M ⊗[R] N →[A] P`, compose it with the canonical
151: bilinear map `M →[A] N →[R] M ⊗[R] N` to form a bilinear map `M →[A] N →[R] P`. -/
152: @[simps]
153: def lcurry : (M ⊗[R] N →ₗ[A] P) →ₗ[B] M →ₗ[A] N →ₗ[R] P where
154:   toFun := curry
155:   map_add' _ _ := rfl
156:   map_smul' _ _ := rfl
157: 
158: /-- Heterobasic version of `TensorProduct.lift.equiv`:
159: 
160: A linear equivalence constructing a linear map `M ⊗[R] N →[A] P` given a
161: bilinear map `M →[A] N →[R] P` with the property that its composition with the
162: canonical bilinear map `M →[A] N →[R] M ⊗[R] N` is the given bilinear map `M →[A] N →[R] P`. -/
163: def lift.equiv : (M →ₗ[A] N →ₗ[R] P) ≃ₗ[B] M ⊗[R] N →ₗ[A] P :=
164:   LinearEquiv.ofLinear (uncurry R A B M N P) (lcurry R A B M N P)
165:     (LinearMap.ext fun _ => ext fun x y => lift_tmul _ x y)
166:     (LinearMap.ext fun f => LinearMap.ext fun x => LinearMap.ext fun y => lift_tmul f x y)
167: 
168: /-- Heterobasic version of `TensorProduct.mk`:
169: 
170: The canonical bilinear map `M →[A] N →[R] M ⊗[R] N`. -/
171: @[simps! apply]
172: nonrec def mk (A M N : Type*) [Semiring A]
173:     [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [Module A M] [SMulCommClass R A M]
174:     [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N] : M →ₗ[A] N →ₗ[R] M ⊗[R] N :=
175:   { mk R M N with map_smul' := fun _ _ => rfl }
176: 
177: variable {R A B M N P Q}
178: 
179: /-- The heterobasic version of `mk` coincides with the regular version. -/
180: lemma mk_eq : mk R R M N = TensorProduct.mk R M N := rfl

62: then used a type synonym `f.codomain` for `f : LocalizationMap M S` to instantiate the
63: `R`-algebra structure on `S`. This results in defining ad-hoc copies for everything already

67: To prove most lemmas about a localization map `algebraMap R S` in this file we invoke the
68: corresponding proof for the underlying `CommMonoid` localization map
69: `IsLocalization.toLocalizationMap M S`, which can be found in `GroupTheory.MonoidLocalization`
70: and the namespace `Submonoid.LocalizationMap`.

72: To reason about the localization as a quotient type, use `mk_eq_of_mk'` and associated lemmas.
73: These show the quotient map `mk : R → M → Localization M` equals the surjection
74: `LocalizationMap.mk'` induced by the map `algebraMap : R →+* Localization M`.
